title: linkml-omc-schema
description:
The OMC-JSON document root: a bundle of OMC entities grouped by entity type, mirroring the OMC-JSON `rootObject`. Each property is an array of that entity type, so every entity shape is reachable from the top level.
NOTE: the original OMC-JSON root is a `oneOf` of THREE forms — this bundle, a single bare entity, and a bare array of entities. LinkML's JSON-Schema generator can only emit one tree_root (the bundle); the single-entity and array forms are added by a post-generation step (scripts/root_forms.py) that rewrites the generated schema root to the 3-way `oneOf`.

Any.description: A permissive "any JSON value" type. Used where the umbrella schema must accept arbitrary structure (e.g. functionalProperties, edges) so that top-level validation passes regardless of subtype.
Any.title: Any

Asset.title: Asset

AssetFunction.description: An Asset's function (assetFunction): what role the Asset plays in production. The concrete role is selected by `assetFunctionType` and detailed by `assetFunctionProperties`; each value corresponds to a `subtype` class that, in RDF, is a subclass of this facet carrying those properties directly.

assetFunctionProperties.description: The Asset's type-specific function properties. Opaque (`Any`) in the core schema and GraphQL; the focused schema narrows it per `assetFunctionType` to the matching `subtype` class's property shape. In RDF these properties hang directly off the subtype class, so the bag itself is pruned from OWL.

assetFunctionType.description: The Asset function-facet subtype discriminator. A controlled vocabulary in JSON (AssetFunctionTypeEnum, derived from the `subtype` classes); in RDF the subclass itself encodes the type, so this is pruned from OWL.

AssetFunction.title: AssetFunction

AssetStructure.description: How an Asset's essence is structured, encoded, stored, or carried.

assetStructureProperties.description: The AssetStructure's type-specific properties. Opaque (`Any`) in the core schema and GraphQL; the focused schema narrows it per `assetStructureType`.

assetStructureType.description: The AssetStructure subtype discriminator (AssetStructureTypeEnum, derived from the `subtype` classes: digital.*, physical.*, assetGroup, …). In RDF the subclass encodes the type, so this is pruned from OWL.

description.description: A brief, human-facing description of the entity.

edges.description: The typed relationships (edges) from this entity to others, grouped by relationship. In this CORE schema every entity gets the full `Edges` structure: all relationships are available, each already constrained to its allowed target entity types (per OMC-JSON). Sub-types narrow further by re-ranging this slot via `slot_usage` (e.g. to a constrained Edges subclass).

AssetStructureVersionInfo.description: The version/lineage of an AssetStructure: its number plus derivation, revision and representation links to other AssetStructures. Edged.description: Opt-in mixin contributing the reified `edges` property (the JSON relationship structure). Edge-bearing entities include it (`mixins: [Edged]`); edge-less entities omit it, so they carry no empty `edges`. The `edges` slot is json_only, so in OWL this mixin contributes nothing -- relationships there are direct predicates (see relationships.yaml).
